title: CN board price-limit regime registry v1
description: Validates config/cn_limit_rules.yml — the CITABLE, board-aware, time-versioned record of A-share daily price-limit regimes (masterplan §4.1 / memo §429-431, gate G0.4). This file is METADATA, not a computer: engine/china_microstructure.py remains the canonical limit-width implementation and this registry never feeds it. What it adds is what the code cannot carry — an effective date, a source URL, and an explicit statement of what is NOT encoded. Every rule row is an interval [valid_from, valid_to] per (board, security_status); the intervals tile each board's timeline with no gaps and no overlaps, so 'which regime governed this date' has exactly one answer. Combinations deliberately not encoded are listed in `unencoded` rather than silently absent (nulls printed, never hidden).

limits_from.description: First date this board had a daily price-limit regime at all — the left edge the `ordinary` continuity check tiles from.

st_from.description: Left edge of the `st` series: the first date a risk-warning status could exist on this board. Distinct from limits_from because the ST designation post-dates the main boards' own price limits by sixteen months — back-filling the ST series to the board's birth would assert a rule for a status that did not yet exist. Null means this board declares no ST series at all, and must then appear in `unencoded`.

ipo_windows.description: Newly-listed windows, where the seasoned-name rule above does not govern. Kept SEPARATE from `rules` so a consumer that only knows about seasoned names cannot accidentally read an IPO window as the daily regime.

rule.description: no_limit = no daily price limit for the first `sessions` sessions. first_day_collar / informational rows record that a special first-day mechanism applied WITHOUT asserting its numeric form — the exact call-auction and temporary-halt mechanics are exchange-rulebook detail this registry deliberately does not encode.

unencoded.description: (board, security_status) combinations this registry does NOT claim to cover, each with a reason. An honest null beats a plausible guess: a fabricated width here would be cited as a fact.

source.description: Per-row citable URL. A regime with no source is not citable and does not belong here.
